label: Episode 02
title: Pretraining a GPT from scratch in PyTorch
subtitle: From random tokens to short stories in a first training run on a laptop, with a tokenizer, the next-token objective, a training loop and evaluation written from scratch.
more: Today, we pretrain our GPT on TinyStories, starting with a word-level tokenizer and the next-token objective, with cross-entropy as the loss. label: Episode 04
title: KV cache from scratch in PyTorch
subtitle: We add a KV cache to our model, so it runs each new token on its own and not the whole story again, and we check and time it on the CPU and the GPU.
more: Our model runs the whole story through all its blocks for each token it writes, so this time we give it a KV cache, which keeps the keys and values of the earlier tokens. title: Constrained decoding: structured LLM output
subtitle: Nothing is trained. Before each token inside a query's name, our agent's graph role masks the tokens that would take the name off a list, and we measure two lists, the graph's names and the task's words.

label: Episode 27
title: Speculative decoding from scratch
subtitle: A draft guesses the next few tokens, and our agent checks them in the pass that writes its own, so it writes what greedy decoding writes in fewer passes. Two drafts, prompt lookup and a small model trained for thirty minutes, measured on the agent's tasks.
more: In this episode, our agent writes its answers word for word as before, in fewer passes of the model. A pass on the Mac's GPU costs about the same for a few tokens as for one, so a cheap draft guesses the next few tokens, and the model checks them in the pass that writes its own, keeping the guesses up to the first it disagrees with. We build speculative decoding from scratch, with two drafts: prompt lookup, which guesses what the text copies for nothing, and a small model of four layers, trained for thirty minutes on the agent's tasks. subtitle: We look inside our agent while it copies a name into a query, with each head's attention written out, the logit lens, and a page of our own, then turn the heads that look at the name off to see what they do.
more: In this episode, we look inside our GPT while its graph role copies a name from its task into a Cypher query. We write attention out by hand to keep each head's weights, put the logit lens on the residual stream to see each layer's guess at the next token, and build a page of our own to look at all 144 heads on a prompt. A head in the last layer puts 92 percent of its attention on the name in the task, and the name shows up in the last layer alone. For the okapi, that head looks at the right token, and the model can't write it inside the quotes.
